newsitem.title: USA: U.S. DOE Deputy Secretary Curtis resigns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DOE Deputy Secretary Curtis resigns.

text.p: U.S. Energy Department Deputy Secretary Charles Curtis resigned from his post on Wednesday, the department announced Thursday.
Energy Secretary Frederico Pena said President Clinton has nominated Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairwoman Elizabeth Moler to fill the Curtis vacancy.
Pena said in a statement he deeply regretted Curtis' resignation.
"Charles Curtis has had a lasting impact on our nation's energy and national security policies, and I wish him the very best in his future endeavors," Pena said.
Curtis served as deputy secretary since August 1995 and was under secretary of energy since February 1994.

Moler joined the FERC in 1988. Before that, she served as senior counsel to the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and worked for the late Sen. Henry Jackson and for Sen. J. Bennett Johnston.
"I could not be more pleased with this nomination, and I look forward to having Betsy join the DOE team," Pena said.
